short: The Lincoln engineer who built the first tank and was legally credited as its inventor.
full:
William Ashbee Tritton was managing director of William Foster and Co. of Lincoln, an agricultural engineering firm making tractors and threshing machines, when the Landships Committee came looking for someone who could actually build what it had been arguing about. Work began at Foster's Wellington Foundry in August 1915. When bought-in American Bullock tracks kept coming off, Tritton designed a riveted plate track of his own that worked, and the No. 1 Lincoln Machine — Little Willie — ran in September 1915 with it fitted.

With Walter Gordon Wilson he then produced Mother, the rhomboid prototype that became the Mark I, and Foster's went on building tanks for the rest of the war. Tritton designed the Medium Mark A Whippet himself as a fast machine to follow the heavies through a breach. He was knighted in February 1917, and in 1919 the Royal Commission on Awards to Inventors named him and Wilson jointly as the inventors of the tank, dividing an award of £15,000 between them. He stayed at Foster's until 1939.
